title.narrative: Third Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan with a Cat DDO

description.narrative: The development objectives of the Third Disaster Risk Management Development Policy Loan in Colombia intend to strengthen the Government of Colombia's program to manage risk resulting from adverse natural events, including disease outbreaks. It supports additional reforms in three policy areas: (a) promoting the further development of disaster risk management (DRM) and climate change policies; (b) strengthening the country's fiscal resilience to disaster, climate and public health risks; and (c) promoting sectoral and subnational co-responsibility in DRM and climate change adaptation. The program will deepen policy reforms by: (a) promoting co-responsibility across sectors, territories and government levels and entities; and (b) expanding disaster risk financing at the national, subnational and sectoral levels, as a key component of contingent liability management and consequently of fiscal management. The operation will also define and develop public policy actions to address climate variability; mitigate climate change by controlling deforestation and promoting the sustainable use of forestry resources; and contribute to mainstreaming disaster and climate risk in the development and operation of multimodal transport and housing infrastructure. Critically, in the context of the COVID-19 crisis and other public health threats driven by climate change, the program supports the formulation of a new Ten-Year Public Health Plan, to be incorporated into disaster planning and informed by lessons learned during the pandemic.
To strengthen the Government of Colombia's program to manage risk resulting from adverse natural events, including disease outbreaks

title.narrative: 5. Percentage of approved territorial development plans incorporating disaster risk management that are published through technology platforms developed by IGAC

comment.narrative: IGAC reported that 280 municipal land use plans (POTs) have integrated disaster risk management (DRM) as per Decree 1807 of 2014, achieving 25.3% of all municipal POTs nationwide. This represents 63% completion towards the target of 40% of municipalities. These POTs are accessible via IGAC's platforms, notably the Colombia OT platform. However, challenges remain, including incomplete DRM studies and the lengthy, costly process of updating POTs. IGAC is enhancing access to cartographic information, but compliance responsibility lies with municipalities.

title.narrative: 1.2. Percentage of national territory covered by subnational profiles strengthened through the incorporation of climate variability analytics

comment.narrative: IGAC reported achieving the target in 2023 by completing 89 characterizations of subnational territories for the multipurpose cadaster and two National Natural Parks (corresponding to 38,728,933 hectares, or 34.5% of the national territory) that incorporate a climate variability component, published at www.Colombiaot.gov.co. These characterizations are the basis for the updating of the land use plans (POTs). This was enabled by the development of an innovative methodology to incorporate climate change into subnational characterizations, which combines baseline information with other data (legal context, occupation, socioeconomic and sectoral processes, municipal ecosystems, sources of risk and climate variability).

title.narrative: 1.2. Percentage of national territory covered by subnational profiles strengthened through the incorporation of climate variability analytics

comment.narrative: In 2023, IGAC achieved its target by completing 89 characterizations of subnational territories for the multipurpose cadaster, covering 38,728,933 hectares or 34.5% of Colombia's national territory. These characterizations, which include a climate variability component, are essential for updating land use plans (POTs). This was made possible through an innovative methodology that integrates climate change considerations with baseline and other relevant data. By 2025, IGAC developed 15 more characterizations, each with a document and geodatabase, increasing the coverage to 36.18% (40,619,037 hectares) across 391 municipalities and two National Natural Parks. IGAC is working on strategies to keep these characterizations updated and publicly accessible.

Significant achievements were noted in the Amazon region, where deforestation fell to 44,256 hectares in 2023, the lowest in 23 years, and in CaquetÃ¡, which saw a 34% reduction. These improvements are attributed to initiatives like the Comprehensive Plan for Deforestation Containment and the "Conservar Paga" mechanism. Although the 2024 deforestation rate is not yet available, an increase is anticipated, despite 2021-2023 being the period with the lowest rates in 23 years. CaquetÃ¡ and the Amazon region currently have the highest deforestation alerts.

title.narrative: 2. Number of hectares affected by deforestation (compared to 2019 baseline)

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Environment (MinAmbiente) reported that the " Monitoring of Forest Area and Deforestation in Colombia 2023 - Report 2023" by IDEAM, published in July 2024, recorded 79,256 hectares of deforestation. This reflects a 36% reduction compared to 2022 (123,517 hectares) and a 50% decrease from the 2019 baseline (158,894 hectares). Notable achievements include the Amazon region, where deforestation dropped from 144,019 hectares in 2017 (the highest in the last 23 years) to 44,256 hectares in 2023 (the lowest in 23 years), and CaquetÃ¡, which saw a 34% decrease, from 19,193 hectares in 2022 to 12,647 hectares in 2023. Key initiatives driving these results include the Comprehensive Plan for Deforestation Containment and the "Conservar Paga" mechanism, which involves communities in deforestation control efforts. Several factors can influence deforestation figures, including the impact of El NiÃ±o, which could affect the reduction trend for 2024.

title.narrative: 3.3. Percentage of households with female recipients participating in Families in Action program that are eligible to receive unconditional extraordinary or ordinary cash transfer following a disaster

comment.narrative: The Department for Social Prosperity (DPS) reported progress toward the end target, reaching 90% of households with female recipients by November 2023. DPS noted that it would no longer report on this indicator as it had concluded the implementation of the Families in Action (Familias en Acción) program and transitioned to the Citizen Income (Renta Ciudadana) program as per the guidelines outlined in the National Development Plan (PND) 2022-26. The Citizen Income Program represents an adaptive and flexible social protection approach. It aims to provide support to vulnerable populations, enabling them to enhance their resilience and improve their livelihoods. This program emphasizes the importance of strengthening the well-being and socio-economic conditions of those in need. In the context of future implementation support missions, DPS will report on the implementation of the Citizen Income program.
